synthesis: Finite zero verification composes a lower count of critical-line witnesses with an independent exhaustive count for the same bounded region; equality leaves no room for additional off-line zeros. Because the comparison uses cardinality rather than refined ordinates, a later count-oriented implementation can discard unnecessary location detail after rigorously determining a sign change.
source_support: Bombieri states the argument-principle total, critical-line sign-change count, and equality certificate; the Lehmer historical span records Hutchinson's at-least-138 sign changes matched to Backlund's exactly-138 rectangle count; Platt-Trudgian explicitly omit high-precision isolation and storage after detecting a sign change and retain only its count.
nonparaphrase_operation: Projects two different witness representations to a shared integer invariant, then identifies refined zero location as information the equality proof does not consume.
limits: The Platt-Trudgian span supplies the information-discarding optimization, not its surrounding global completeness argument. Sign changes alone are nonexhaustive, equality applies only to a matched region and certified evaluations, and no finite-height result proves RH globally.
quality_reason: All three parents support distinct necessary parts of the relation, and the synthesis preserves the separation between lower-bound witnesses, exhaustive counting, and implementation-level data reduction.

synthesis: A computed Hardy-Z value has a certified sign only when its magnitude dominates the applicable absolute-error envelope. That margin induces an adaptive policy: settle large-margin samples cheaply, defer ambiguous samples to a more accurate method or shifted points, and treat shifts as a changed sampling protocol in later statistics.
source_support: The SWAC span compares approximate values with a remainder estimate, refines adjacent intervals, and sends the remaining ambiguous case to a smaller-remainder method; the CYBER span separates interpolation, Riemann-Siegel truncation, and arithmetic contributions and uses conservative operational bounds; the later statistics span tries small shifts before method B and explicitly warns that shifted and unshifted statistics are not strictly accumulable.
nonparaphrase_operation: Turns a one-sided error inequality into both an exact-sign interface and a routing rule, then propagates the routing intervention into the provenance of aggregate measurements.
limits: Every envelope is method-, machine-, and range-specific. A shifted evaluation is not an independent implementation, empirical agreement does not prove protocol equivalence, and certified sample signs do not themselves establish an exhaustive zero count.
quality_reason: The relation is concrete across all three parents: uncertainty controls computational effort, while the method used to resolve uncertainty changes what downstream aggregation is licensed.

synthesis: Critical-line evaluation can reduce runtime successively by choosing the Riemann-Siegel saddle scale and by precomputing derivative-based Taylor tables for repeated correction evaluation; proof use then requires a separate conservative accounting of series, interpolation, coefficient-cutoff, and arithmetic errors. These are modular stages rather than evidence that one implementation validates another.
source_support: Pugh's formula span gives the square-root-length main sum and correction hierarchy, while the Taylor-table span gives the p-to-z derivative scaling and offline Maple coefficient generation. The CYBER span exhibits method-specific analytic, interpolation, and machine-error envelopes, and Platt-Trudgian show that rigorous multiprecision, sampling density, and algorithm choice materially change a processed-height throughput comparison.
nonparaphrase_operation: Separates analytic compression, amortized symbolic preprocessing, and numerical certification into interfaces whose costs and proof obligations can be audited independently.
limits: The Taylor coefficient cutoff has no uniform remainder bound in its span, and the later error envelopes do not certify Pugh's tables. Historical throughput figures are not cross-machine invariants and depend on sampling, precision, hardware, algorithm, and rigor.
quality_reason: Each parent supports a different rung of a precise computational decomposition, and the synthesis explicitly blocks the otherwise invalid transfer of later certification claims to the earlier implementation.

synthesis: Batch evaluation and isolated evaluation optimize different costs: precomputation can amortize an FFT-style method over many Hardy-Z values without reducing the cost of one requested value, while processed-height-per-GHz-hour measures campaign throughput without normalizing sampling density, precision, or certification work.
source_support: Pugh identifies the main cosine sum as the singleton cost center and states that precomputation-based batch methods do not improve one evaluation. Platt-Trudgian report a processed-half-line-length rate and attribute large differences to FFT versus direct Riemann-Siegel evaluation, samples per zero, and rigorous multiprecision versus hardware floating point.
nonparaphrase_operation: Factorizes total cost into setup, per-batch, and per-query components, then audits which of those components a hardware-normalized throughput metric leaves hidden.
limits: The parents provide no controlled head-to-head benchmark and establish no universally superior algorithm. Pugh's faster singleton approximation is only proposed future work, and any implementation would require its own error analysis.
quality_reason: The comparison is supported by explicit cost-center and metric evidence rather than a title-level analogy, and it keeps performance objectives separate from mathematical correctness.

synthesis: The proposed discovery lineage is unsupported: Lehmer's recurrence argument targets repeated cancellation and low extrema, whereas the later source describes a close pair found in a large zero computation and does not attribute that discovery to the cancellation heuristic. The later close-pair recomputation and Lehmer-inequality certificate form a valid two-parent pipeline, but the cited early parent cannot be joined to it as claimed.
source_support: The Lehmer span proposes remote searches for recurrence of a term-cancellation phenomenon and explicitly does not discuss discovery of close pairs. The later provenance span attributes the selected close pair to van de Lune, te Riele, and Winter and concentrates precision near it; the certificate span combines bounded contributions to g_K with the scaled gap to verify the Lehmer threshold.
nonparaphrase_operation: A valid operation would map a discovered gap through x=2 gamma and a one-sided environmental enclosure to the scalar Lehmer inequality; the candidate instead prepends an unestablished causal bridge from a different search heuristic.
limits: The certified pair is neither a globally optimal gap nor an RH result, and the early cancellation recurrence concerns neither RH counterexamples nor recurrence of close pairs. Removing the unsupported parent would be a materially different synthesis assignment.
quality_reason: Not all cited parents support the asserted relation. Accepting it would convert temporal adjacency and a broad search motif into a historical and mathematical connection absent from the exact evidence.

synthesis: Both the static Lehmer-pair test and the heat-flow zero dynamics make a local gap configuration depend on the surrounding zeros: the former multiplies the gap scale by an all-other-zero reciprocal-square interaction, while the latter moves each real zero by a principal-value inverse-distance interaction. This is a structural comparison, not a derivation of either formula from the other.
source_support: The Lehmer criterion defines the gap and the all-other-zero term g_k and transfers a qualifying pair to a lower bound for Lambda. The infinite-pair argument reparameterizes the normalized product and conditionally transfers vanishing certified gaps to bounds tending to zero. Rodgers-Tao rigorously state the inverse-distance zero ODE, while labeling the relaxation estimate and unrenormalized Hamiltonian discussion heuristic or formal.
nonparaphrase_operation: Compares two different reductions of an infinite zero configuration: a static scalar certificate for a selected pair and a time-dependent principal-value interaction law for every zero, with the normalized Lehmer parameter controlling the conditional limit passage.
limits: The static criterion and ODE have different hypotheses and are not equivalent. The infinite-sequence conclusion is conditional on certified Lehmer pairs with the required limit; the relaxation rate and divergent Hamiltonian discussion are not rigorous results in the cited span.
quality_reason: The reciprocal interaction structures give a concrete mathematical comparison, and the synthesis preserves the parents' incompatible proof status instead of treating the dynamical heuristic as justification for the static theorem.

synthesis: Finite computation constrains the de Bruijn-Newman phase boundary through two opposite theorem-mediated interfaces: exhaustive RH verification beyond a stated height feeds a threshold theorem to give an upper bound for Lambda, while a certified exceptional pair feeds a pair theorem to give a lower bound.
source_support: Platt-Trudgian insert their verified height into a published threshold to obtain Lambda at most 0.2 and state that the next threshold was not reached. The Lehmer-pair source gives a pair-specific negative lower bound and only conditionally reaches Lambda at least zero from infinitely many qualifying pairs; the continuation span applies that theorem to a certified pair and labels further improvement by extended computation as a forecast.
nonparaphrase_operation: Tracks the direction of implication through two distinct transfer maps: coverage height maps monotonically to an upper phase-boundary constraint, while normalized local zero geometry maps to a lower constraint.
limits: The inputs and transfer theorems are not interchangeable. The achieved height gives neither the next upper threshold nor RH, a finite pair gives only its stated lower bound, and predicted future pairs or improvements are not established facts.
quality_reason: All parents support the two-sided comparison, and the synthesis makes the opposite inequality directions and epistemic statuses explicit rather than collapsing them into generic numerical evidence.

synthesis: The two programs compress root location into counts with opposite logical polarity: for zeta, equality between critical-line witnesses and an independent regional total proves absence of additional off-line zeros there; for a Jensen polynomial, a complete real-root count below the degree proves existence of at least one nonreal root.
source_support: Bombieri states the argument-principle total, sign-change witnesses, and equality conclusion. The Jensen-polynomial span states the Sturm sign-variation count and uses it to decide whether all roots are real, while the implementation span describes a containing negative-real interval, interval enlargement, precision-sensitive sign patterns, and Newton location only as an extra check.
nonparaphrase_operation: Dualizes a cardinality comparison: equality closes an exclusion proof in one setting, whereas a deficit supplies an existential obstruction in the other, without transferring either counting theorem's hypotheses.
limits: The zeta certificate is analytic and region-bounded. The polynomial conclusion requires the stated Sturm hypotheses, an interval containing every real root, and trustworthy endpoint signs; the reported finite-precision recovery of expected patterns is a diagnostic, not an exact-arithmetic certificate by itself.
quality_reason: The opposite equality-versus-deficit logic is explicit and reusable, while the synthesis keeps analytic and algebraic mechanisms and their numerical obligations separate.

synthesis: A cheap computational policy should remain provisional when its ordering changes under the quantity that ultimately matters: Landau's score and the finite R0 calculation rank admissible polynomials differently, while Gram-block data show that an outer-first search order effective on common short blocks becomes inefficient on rare longer blocks. Downstream evaluation or observed conditional structure must therefore be allowed to rerank or branch.
source_support: The polynomial span reports contrary Landau and Kadiri rankings, a wider reranking of many near-surrogate-optimal candidates, and a degree-16 downstream winner without global optimality. The Gram-block span reports success of the existing strategy for lengths two through five and a different positional tendency from length six onward, including only one outer placement among 93 length-seven blocks.
nonparaphrase_operation: Places objective mismatch and conditional distribution shift under one bounded decision rule: retain candidates or search options generated cheaply, but condition the final ordering on the expensive target or the empirically relevant stratum.
limits: The mathematical objects and policies are not equivalent. The polynomial pool is finite and heuristic, the final annealing objective is unspecified in the span, and the block statistics are range-dependent, shift-confounded, and not a proof of an optimal search policy.
quality_reason: The comparison is grounded in an observed ranking reversal and an observed strategy crossover, so it yields a concrete computational design principle rather than generic topical co-occurrence.
